name: Mission San Buenaventura
history: St. Junípero Serra founded Mission San Buenaventura on 31 March 1782, the ninth mission in Alta California and the last founded in his lifetime. It had been planned as the third, but was delayed for lack of a military escort. Its first church burned in 1793. Between 1805 and 1815 the Chumash people built an aqueduct system for the mission. Pope Francis named it a basilica in 2020.
arch: A whitewashed mission church with a red-tiled gable front and a stepped bell tower with a domed cap.
features: The mission is a California Historical Landmark.
Of the original mission, only the church and its garden remain. Its Ventureño Chumash name is mitsqanaqan̓.

look.d: The stepped tower rises beside the simple front.
A fountain stands in the garden before the mission.

fun: Serra himself dedicated it, one of only six missions he personally dedicated.
journal: Serra's last mission. White walls, red tile, the Pacific a few blocks away.
